analysis.title: Zuck'd: Tech Wrecks As AI Credit Cracks Widen; Bonds Panic-Bid, Bitcoin & Bullion Battered
key_insights: AI-related CDS spreads rose further on funding concerns. META was the focal point after earnings showed negative free cash flow and higher spending plans. NDX fell over 3% and SPX fell 1.5%, while the Dow and Russell 2000 were roughly unchanged.

Treasuries rallied sharply. The 10Y UST yield fell back below 5.00% to a one-month low, its biggest one-day decline since Aug 2024, and broke its 50-day moving average for the first time since June. The 5Y and 7Y yields fell about 20bps.

The French 10Y yield rose above 5.10%, the highest since June 2002. It traded 50bps above Italy and above the US 10Y for the first time since 2013. France CDS passed 100bps for the first time since 2012.

Goldman's futures desk says trend followers are buyers in every bond market it models. They are set to buy $18mm DV01 this week, up to $27mm if yields keep falling, and $55mm DV01 over a month, about a third of their simulated net short.

RBC strategists link the Treasury bid to rising odds that Democrats win both chambers in the midterms. They say a growing consensus sees Democratic outperformance as negative for the AI narrative and bullish for rates.

Barclays credit analyst Andrew Keches says META's equity announcement is positive for credit in isolation, but the 14C filing suggests very large spending ambitions. Barclays expects a META bond deal in the near term, which will weigh on spreads.
Data-center CDS returned to record wides, CRWV yields were back above 15%, hyperscaler credit risk kept rising, and broad credit is at cycle wides across the quality spectrum.

Goldman's Privorotsky: AI weakness reprices the capex cycle, eases pressure on prospective issuance and increasingly becomes a growth shock. The thing creating the equity problem helps solve the rates problem.
LRCX gave weak guidance, META reported negative FCF and funding concerns, and TSLA cut capex. Mag7 was not a safe haven. Equal-weight SPX had its best day relative to SPX since July 2024.

Goldman Prime Brokerage had Fundamental L/S down 1.1%, Systematics down 1.2% and Multi-Strats down 1.4%, the first time since COVID all three fell more than 1% on the same day. The GS HF VIP pair (GSTHVIPP) fell about 4.2%, its worst day since 2011, and is down 10.4% month to date.
Goldman's desk flow was 11% better for sale, with long-only sell skew of 22% and hedge funds 9% better for sale. Kaplan saw zero signs of offense being played around the AI theme.

Goldman baskets: High Beta Momentum (GSPRHIMO) erased all YTD gains, AI Winners vs AI at Risk (GSPUARTI) had its 5th worst session of the year, and AI names underperformed by 750bps of dispersion. Semis, memory, neoclouds and optical networking were hit.

WTI traded up to resistance near $100, near its Iran-war highs, on Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, IRGC strikes on vessels in the Persian Gulf and reports of US/Israeli plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the midterms. Diesel rose despite a Russian diesel shipment to the US.
S&P Global's Burkhard attributes oil's rise since early September to constrained logistics, less Iranian supply, falling inventories, renewed Chinese buying and record tanker rates.
Gold fell below $4,100 and bitcoin gave back the prior day's gains, finding support near $81k. The dollar ended modestly lower.

The article concludes the market has moved from treating the AI selloff as a positioning wash to treating it as a growth problem. Rate-hike odds fell, and Treasuries rallied into an oil spike, which it reads as oil being a growth threat rather than an inflation threat.

market_movers.rationale: Earnings showed negative free cash flow and higher spending plans. Credit risk spiked, and Barclays expects a bond deal in the near term that will weigh on spreads.
Weak guidance contributed to the semiconductor selloff.
Slashed capex, which pushed TSLA credit risk higher.
Yields back above 15%, described as the market's new beta barometer.
Strong free cash flow and modest infrastructure spending make it a defensive hedge, but it trades at a premium while growing more slowly than peers.

sector_views.rationale: Selling was concentrated in tech megacaps, semis, memory, neoclouds and optical networking on funding and capex concerns.
Investors rotated into defensive sectors as recent AI winners were sold.
Oil is supported by Middle East escalation and logistics constraints, but sellers and buyers both lack conviction.

earnings_insights: META (reported 10/22): negative free cash flow and higher spending plans, with a 14C filing and an equity announcement. Barclays expects a bond deal soon.
LRCX (reported): weak guidance, per the article. No figures given.
TSLA (reported): capex cut, per the article. No figures given.

Highest since June 2002, above the US 10Y for the first time since 2013 and 50bps above Italy.
Back at Iran-war highs on Middle East escalation and supply logistics.
Sold off despite the bond rally and softer dollar.

crypto_views: Bitcoin gave back all of the prior day's gains and found support near $81k again.

CTA short covering could extend the Treasury rally.
French and European bond crisis spillover.
Oil spike from Middle East escalation, including renewed US/Israeli strikes on Iran after the midterms.
Democratic midterm gains leading to more AI regulation.
Credit already at cycle wides across the quality spectrum.

The US ordered some personnel and family members to leave embassies in Saudi Arabia, and Aramco planned to evacuate its HQ.
Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries and a US-Russia diesel supply deal.
French political and bond market stress, with the Le Pen respite reversed.
US midterm elections in two weeks, with analysts linking Middle East escalation and oil prices to them.

tension_points.bull_case: Equity issuance and strong demand for AI could support spending. The Barclays analyst reads META's equity announcement positively for credit in isolation.
tension_points.bear_case: Spending ambitions look very large, META will need both credit and equity markets, a bond deal is expected, and credit is at cycle wides.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A META bond deal that widens spreads further would confirm the bear case.

tension_points.bull_case: Bonds are bid on growth anxiety, European safe-haven flows and lower AI-related supply.
tension_points.bear_case: The move was exaggerated by a CTA short squeeze and partly reflects European flows, not domestic growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Yields falling further would extend the CTA buying ($27mm DV01 this week) and the squeeze.
